messages.author: 4b85f40a0f87fa84
messages.subject: total covariate effect in zero-inflated/hurdle models
parts:
Hi all,
I am fitting some zero-inflated count models where both the zero-inflation probability (psi) and the mean for the counts (lam) are functions of the same covariate. So, something like this:
logit(psi) = a_psi _b_psi * X
log(lam) = a_lam + b_lam * X
Now I am interested in the total effect of X on Y (Y being my zero-inflated counts). Is there a way to calculate that from estimates of b_psi and b_lam?
A quick google search showed that there are marginalized versions of these models that directly estimate the total effect of X on the mean of the zero-inflated counts. But I'd like to know if there is a way to determine this effect using estimates from the regular ZIP model. And, if there is a way to do so, how does that change if you have a hurdle model rather than a ZIP model.
Any thoughts much appreciated!
Thanks
Rahel

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: total covariate effect in zero-inflated/hurdle models
parts:
Dear Rahel,

I don't really have an answer for this, but I wonder about the estimability of such a model: unless you have replicates in the second stage of the model (for log(lam)), intuitively I feel that estimability depends exclusively on the fact that you have a logit for the first stage and a log for the second. I wonder how stable the inferences from such a model are likely to be ?

Best regards  ---- Marc

messages.author: 4b85f40a0f87fa84
messages.subject: Re: total covariate effect in zero-inflated/hurdle models
parts:
Hi Marc,
we actually do have replication on the count level. This is a situation where there is (ecologically) no way around including the covariate on both model levels. I do realize didn't phrase my post very well, though; I am fitting a hurdle model, so that I'm not trying to separate out structural from count zeros, just modeling the two components separately (and there is no way around that for the sake of model fit).
Best
Rahel
